title: A ring-buffer event logger: report in time order

prereqs.why: This is the structure itself: an array, two indices, and a modulo that turns it into a circle.
The slots are a vector sized once in the constructor and then only ever written through, never grown.
Three files are compiled separately and linked, so a signature that does not match its declaration is a link error rather than a compile error.
Every index here is taken modulo the capacity, and the one that is not is the bug that reads past the end.

statement:
**Milestone 3 of 3.** The events are stamped with when they *happened*, and
they do not arrive in that order. The logger has to report them in it.

### What is carried forward

Your `ring_buffer.hpp` and `ring_buffer.cpp` arrive as you left them in
milestone 2, and nothing more is asked of them. This milestone is in
`main.cpp`, which is **yours to edit from here on** — the `report` branch is
empty.

### The commands

The first line is the capacity. Every line after it is one command.

```
push <at> <text>   add an event; <at> is a whole number, <text> is one word
pop                remove and print the oldest event, or print `empty`
size               print `<held>/<capacity>`
dump               print every event held, oldest arrival first, or `(none)`
```

`push` prints nothing when it works. A command that is not one of these is
ignored, and so is a malformed one.

```
overwrite on|off   turn overwriting on or off
dropped            print how many events have been dropped
report             print the events held, earliest timestamp first
```

### What `report` has to do

- Print one line per event held, `<at> <text>`, in increasing order of `at`.
- Two events with the same `at` keep the order they **arrived** in. `at(0)` is
  the oldest arrival, so that order is the one the buffer is already in.
- Print `(none)` when the buffer is empty.
- It must not change the buffer: a `report` followed by a `dump` prints the
  same events, in the buffer's own order.
- Timestamps may be negative, and may be larger than fits in 32 bits.

### The sample

```
4
push 30 c
push 10 a
push 20 b
report          ->    10 a
                      20 b
                      30 c
dump            ->    30 c
                      10 a
                      20 b
```

### How it is checked

The cases are this milestone's, milestone 2's and milestone 1's. The logger
has to do everything it ever did, plus this.
hints: `report` needs the events in a place you can sort, and the buffer already offers one event at a time through `at(i)`. Copy them into a `std::vector<Event>` first; sorting the buffer itself would break the rule that `report` leaves it alone.
`std::sort` is not enough. Two events stamped the same have to come out in the order they arrived, and `std::sort` is free to swap equal elements. `std::stable_sort` is the one that promises not to.
The comparison is on the timestamp only: `a.at < b.at`. Comparing the text as well, or using `<=`, is how a tie stops being a tie. Remember `(none)` for the empty buffer — there is a case for it.

cases.stdin:
4
push 30 c
push 10 a
push 20 b
report
dump

3
report
overwrite on
push 50 e
push 10 a
push 70 g
push 20 b
report
